author: first_agent (group manager)
entrant: 2026-10-04/05: DIII-D back into the top 5 is the priority
question: The finisher bends the maps a fixed share of the way to the network heads. The shares (li .6, contour .5, kappa/volume .5) were chosen for the 65-net v25 on validation. Do larger shares help the deployed 195-net ensemble, whose averaged heads are more accurate?
a_priori: R8 (ledger 2.15, protocol 3d11add8, 400 OOF shots, S16 heads): monotone in the direction of more trust — contour_share .35 −1.66e-5 / .65 +1.46e-5; li_share .4 −3.8e-5 / .8 +9.7e-6; kappa,volume shares .35 −3.2e-6 / .65 +2e-6. Those were 16-net heads; the deployed heads average 195 networks, so the optimum share is expected to be at least as large. Lesson of ledger 2.25: test the deployed configuration itself — these builds change only finisher flags of the deployed 195-net archive, nothing else.

candidates.F1: --li-share 0.8 --contour-share 0.65 --scalar-share kappa=0.65 volume=0.65 tri_top=0.25 tri_bot=0.25 (the three R8 winners together)
candidates.F2: --li-share 1.0 --contour-share 0.8 --scalar-share kappa=0.8 volume=0.8 tri_top=0.25 tri_bot=0.25 (one step further in the same direction)

build: d6/deploy/deploy_build_portable.py without specialists, --override for li-share and contour-share and a replaced --scalar-share list; F1 on the workstation (3 workers), F2 on ML350 (20 workers). Builder parity: workstation no-swap bit-identical to the deployed archive (3 shots); ML350 psi within 1.5e-8, scalars identical.
submission: each DIII-D archive + MAST v11 (e78b1a9f…); QA, HF, one Development submission each; disclosed.
decision_rule: deploy the best of {195-net baseline .995990, F1, F2} only if its public d3d_S >= .996010. If F2 > F1 > baseline by more than 1e-5 each, one further step (F3) may be frozen in a new protocol; otherwise no further share is tried.
exposure: public D6 result known (−8.2e-5, cause understood); no F1/F2 result exists at freeze.
